## Purpose

This report compares the student-prepared dataset,
`armed_conflict_final_data.csv`, with the independently prepared AI dataset,
`armed_conflict_health_data_AI.csv`. The comparison evaluates dimensions,
country-year coverage, variable names, missing values, and cell-level values.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

student_path <- "../Data/Processed/armed_conflict_final_data.csv"
ai_path <- "../Data/Processed/armed_conflict_health_data_AI.csv"

student_data <- read_csv(student_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
ai_data <- read_csv(ai_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Dataset structure

```{r}
structure_summary <- tibble(
  dataset = c("Student final dataset", "AI final dataset"),
  rows = c(nrow(student_data), nrow(ai_data)),
  columns = c(ncol(student_data), ncol(ai_data)),
  countries = c(n_distinct(student_data$iso), n_distinct(ai_data$iso)),
  minimum_year = c(min(student_data$year), min(ai_data$year)),
  maximum_year = c(max(student_data$year), max(ai_data$year)),
  duplicate_country_years = c(
    sum(duplicated(student_data[c("iso", "year")])),
    sum(duplicated(ai_data[c("iso", "year")]))
  )
)

kable(structure_summary)
```

Both datasets contain 3,720 observations, 17 variables, 186 countries, and 20
years (2000--2019). Neither dataset contains duplicate country-year records.

## Variable names and order

```{r}
variable_comparison <- tibble(
  position = seq_len(max(ncol(student_data), ncol(ai_data))),
  student_dataset = names(student_data),
  ai_dataset = names(ai_data)
)

kable(variable_comparison)
```

The datasets contain the same substantive variables. There are two structural
differences:

1. The student dataset calls the conflict indicator `armed_conflict`, whereas
   the AI dataset calls it `conflict`.
2. The variables appear in a different column order. Column order does not
   affect the data values when variables are matched by name.

## Country-year coverage

```{r}
student_keys <- student_data |> select(iso, year)
ai_keys <- ai_data |> select(iso, year)

key_summary <- tibble(
  comparison = c(
    "Country-years only in student dataset",
    "Country-years only in AI dataset"
  ),
  records = c(
    nrow(anti_join(student_keys, ai_keys, by = c("iso", "year"))),
    nrow(anti_join(ai_keys, student_keys, by = c("iso", "year")))
  )
)

kable(key_summary)
```

The two datasets have identical country-year coverage.

## Cell-level comparison

For a direct comparison, the conflict variable is given the common name
`conflict`, and both datasets are sorted by country and year. A value is counted
as different if the two datasets contain unequal values or if one value is
missing while the other is not.

```{r}
student_aligned <- student_data |>
  rename(conflict = armed_conflict) |>
  select(all_of(names(ai_data))) |>
  arrange(iso, year)

ai_aligned <- ai_data |>
  arrange(iso, year)

comparison_summary <- map_dfr(names(ai_aligned), function(variable) {
  student_value <- student_aligned[[variable]]
  ai_value <- ai_aligned[[variable]]

  equal_value <-
    (is.na(student_value) & is.na(ai_value)) |
    (!is.na(student_value) & !is.na(ai_value) & student_value == ai_value)

  tibble(
    variable = variable,
    differing_cells = sum(!equal_value),
    missing_student = sum(is.na(student_value)),
    missing_ai = sum(is.na(ai_value))
  )
})

kable(comparison_summary)
```

All values match after aligning the conflict variable name, except for the
`earthquake` and `drought` indicators. Each of these variables differs in 3,132
rows. In the student dataset, these cells are missing (`NA`); in the AI dataset,
they are coded as 0.

```{r}
disaster_cross_tab <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    variable = "earthquake",
    student_value = if_else(
      is.na(student_aligned$earthquake),
      "NA",
      as.character(student_aligned$earthquake)
    ),
    ai_value = if_else(
      is.na(ai_aligned$earthquake),
      "NA",
      as.character(ai_aligned$earthquake)
    )
  ),
  tibble(
    variable = "drought",
    student_value = if_else(
      is.na(student_aligned$drought),
      "NA",
      as.character(student_aligned$drought)
    ),
    ai_value = if_else(
      is.na(ai_aligned$drought),
      "NA",
      as.character(ai_aligned$drought)
    )
  )
) |>
  count(variable, student_value, ai_value, name = "records")

kable(disaster_cross_tab)
```

## Interpretation

The difference results from how country-years without a matching disaster
record were handled after the merge:

- The student dataset retains these unmatched values as `NA`.
- The AI dataset replaces them with 0, interpreting the absence of a matching
  earthquake or drought record as no occurrence of that disaster type.

This is a substantive data-management decision. A value of 0 is appropriate
only if the disaster source can be treated as complete for every included
country-year. If lack of a record might instead mean that disaster information
was unavailable, retaining `NA` is more cautious.

## Conclusion

The two preparation approaches produce the same observations and the same
values for conflict, mortality, and all covariates. Their only data-value
difference is the treatment of unmatched earthquake and drought records. The
preferred version therefore depends on whether the absence of a disaster record
can validly be interpreted as no disaster.
